newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Land claim changes good for all - Canberra.
newsitem.headline: Land claim changes good for all - Canberra.

text.p: Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Wednesday proposed amendments to the Native Title Act would benefit all Australians.
"The government's proposed amendments represent a balance between the interests of all groups and industries with a stake in the Native Title legislation," Anderson told parliament.

"At the same time, as we recognise the particular interests of the aboriginal people, it is in the interest of all Australians to provide greater certainty over land tenure and therefore, investment."
On Tuesday, the government revealed plans to change the act in order to make it more difficult for aboriginal groups to force negotiations on land claims.
Anderson said the changes had won approval from the Minerals Council of Australia and the Western Australian state government.
"The Native Title Act as currently formulated is unworkable to the detriment of all," he said.
"At present, companies are tied up in endless negotiation, which at the end of the day will be of little or no benefit to aboriginal people."
-- Make it clear that the right to negotiate provisions would occur at the same time as state governments were processing applications for mining permits;
-- Improve the process for excluding activities such as exploration and prospecting from the negotiation process; and
-- Provide for more specific criteria to be followed by the arbitrators determining whether aborigines had native title to the land they claim;
-- Allow for earlier ministerial intervention in exceptional cases.
"These amendments will produce a better outcome for all Australians," Anderson said.
The Native Title Act, passed by the former Labor government, allows aboriginal groups to claim title on traditional lands.
Miners and farmers have lobbied the new conservative Liberal-National government to alter the act as it was delaying or preventing mining and other projects from going ahead.

The amendments were released on Tuesday in a discussion paper and will be introduced into parliament when the Native Title Amendment Bill reaches the upper house Senate. Debate is scheduled for early December.
